lines.note: Mendan denotes speaking face to face. The paraphrase visibly reads Gigini cataru; its g spelling is retained rather than changed to suit an expected modern reading. Preſen- continues below.
Cialmente completes preſencialmente, reinforced by vendoſe, seeing one another. Mendanuo to- begins the example whose verb ends on the next row.
Guru completes toguru in Mendanuo toguru. The translation describes speaking together in person, not merely seeing someone at a distance.
The first Menden has Mendan’s meaning by Idem. It remains distinct from the following homograph about land revenue.

runs.text: Varzeas que ſe dão ſem pagar todo

lines.note: The second Menden denotes fields granted without the full yield or revenue payment. Varzeas identifies the land; todo governs the continuation below.
O rendimento completes the payment not owed in full. The statement concerns a remitted land obligation, not a lack of crops.
Mendori is a female bird; italic Meliùs recommends Medori as preferable. The two Japanese forms are alternatives rather than one compound.

runs.text: Couſa que não he pera ver, mal fei-

lines.note: Mendǒna is something not fit to look at or badly made. This stated sense is retained instead of the familiar modern “troublesome”; fei- continues below.
Ta completes mal feita, badly made, followed by &c. This brief row remains the continuation of Mendǒna.
Mendǒni is explicitly labelled an adverb and depends on the preceding adjective. Adu. belongs to the italic grammatical apparatus.
Meneco is a female cat, matched by Gata. Initial me- is meaningful and is not corrected to the unqualified Neco.
Mengio is pardon or privilege, paraphrased Yuruxi nozoqu. The wording covers exemption or release as well as forgiveness; the gi spelling remains unchanged.
Mengio ſuru means granting pardon, permission, or a privilege. The Portuguese licen- continues as ça below.
Ça completes licença. Priuilegio has i rather than the OCR’s extra l and agrees with the visible form in the headword gloss.
A clear caron over final u gives Mengiǔ, not unmarked Mengiu. The gloss identifies a Chinese silk fabric, with Canga used as a textile designation here.
Menjen means before someone or in their presence, paraphrased Vomoteno maye. The Portuguese preſença continues below.
Preſença completes the locution, followed by upright S. for written usage. The label is separate from the italic gloss.
Menji, zuru, ita supplies the principal forms of a verb meaning pardon. Giǔqua begins an example concerning a grave offence.
The grave offence is remitted by commutation to distant exile. Feiq. is an upright citation label; Lib. 1. and Per- belong to the italic reference and translation.

runs.text: dou o grande crime commutando lho em deſter

lines.note: Dou completes Perdou. The Portuguese explains commutation of the great crime to exile; deſter continues below without a securely visible hyphen.
Ro completes deſterro. Sonatani menjite yuruſu means forgiving for the addressee’s sake; a- begins Portuguese amor below.
Mor completes amor, giving “for your sake I forgive.” This closes the second example, not the exile narrative.
This Menjǒ means being in someone’s presence. Menjǒuo mot- starts a polite formula for speaking in person, with motte divided across rows.

Te completes motte, and mǒſubequſoro is translated “I shall speak in person.” Enlargement shows that the trace over final o belongs to the preceding row; the unaccented o and joined Empreſença are retained.
The second Menjǒ is a letter of pardon, paraphrased Yuruxijǒ. It is a separate homophone from the presence expression.
Menmen means each person individually, matched by Cada hum. The repetition is distributive, not duplicated OCR.
Menmiô means face, paraphrased Vomote cauo. The example starts with roman Mẽ-, whose nasal abbreviation does not inherit the Portuguese italics.
Miô completes abbreviated Menmiô; the example describes an exceptionally beautiful face. The printed itçucuxixi, including its unusual final xi, is retained rather than silently regularized.
To completes muito, and bello finishes “very beautiful.” The row closes the facial-appearance example.
Menmit concerns strong or rigorous treatment. Final t remains a historical checked-coda spelling; Vt introduces its application below.
Menmitni ſataſuru describes judging or handling litigation rigorously. Demandas is divided after de without a secure hyphen supplied from its continuation.
Mandas completes demandas; the explanation adds rigour and justice. Provisional justiça typography is not globally recast as long-s/st.
Menmocu first denotes face or appearance. Menmocuno yoi is completed by fito below; this is not the earlier Menbocu entry.
Fito completes “a person of good appearance.” Item introduces a second sense, a professed principle or practice, below.

runs.text: Profißão, ou inſtituto dalgũa couſa. Vt,

lines.note: The second sense is a profession or defining practice. Va- begins Vaga, “our,” in the example about a religious school.
Vaga xǔno menmocuua jiccai nari identifies the school’s practice with ten precepts. Portuguese O que begins the translation; this need not mean the Christian Decalogue.

runs.text: profeßamos em noßa ley he 10. mãdamentos.

lines.note: The translation states that the religion professes ten commandments or precepts. The scan prints 10., not split to; the whole Portuguese statement is italic.

runs.text: Certa pedra precioſa preta que luze co

lines.note: Menǒ is described as a black, shining precious stone. The comparison continues after co without a visible terminal hyphen; no modern mineral identification is substituted.

runs.text: mo azeuiche, ou por ventura he o meſmo aze-

lines.note: Mo completes como: the stone shines like jet or perhaps is jet itself. Meſmo, not moſmo, is visible, and the author’s explicit uncertainty is retained.
Uiche completes azeuiche, jet. This ends the tentative mineral comparison before the eye and nurse entries.
Menotama is the eyeball, matched by Bugalho do olho. Its historical form is not replaced with a modern colloquial equivalent.
Menoto denotes a nurse or child’s attendant, with both Ayo and ama given. The alternatives are not narrowed to one sex or duty.
Menpacu is something clear and apparent to sight, paraphrased Vomote xiroi. The gloss does not supply the later everyday “interesting” sense.
Manifeſta à viſta completes the description as manifest to sight. The two adjectives belong to the same definition.
Menpai, paraphrased Vomoteuo vogamu, means seeing someone with reverence. Re- begins reuerencia on the next row.
Uerencia completes reuerencia; the object is a noble person. Historical u/v and peßoa are retained.

runs.text: Comer feito de farinha de trigo, co-

lines.note: Menrui denotes food made from wheat flour. Comer functions as a noun here; co- introduces the example below.
Mo completes como, with letria as an example of flour-based food. This is genuine body text above the rule, not a catchword.
Menten is meeting or seeing someone, paraphrased Vomote meguru. En- begins encontrarſe across the physical break.
Contrarſe completes encontrarſe com alguem. Final upright S. marks written usage rather than extending the italic definition.

runs.text: Hũas chapas de metal com lauores,

lines.note: Menuqi identifies worked or relief-decorated metal plates. The next rows explain their attachment to sword handles.

runs.text: ou releuo que pegão nos cabos da Catana poror-

lines.note: The plates attach to sword handles as ornament. Compact poror- is retained before nato below; Catana is inside the Portuguese explanation.
Nato completes ornato. The fittings are fastened with straps, completing the same object description rather than starting another item.
Menyet concerns going to see or meet someone. Printed Indo, ver and its punctuation remain unchanged rather than repaired into modern Portuguese.
Alguem completes the object of the visit. S. is an upright written-usage label, separate from the italic gloss.
Menyu is flattery, directly glossed Liſonja. The short entry stands independently before the Buddhist lodging term.

runs.text: Camara, ou caſa em que os Bonzos

lines.note: Menzǒ is a chamber or house for Buddhist monks. The next row specifies sleeping and keeping possessions there; the caron remains.
The monks sleep there and keep belongings or clothing. Printed ofato remains joined; fato is not the English word “fact.”
Meô and attributive meôna are paraphrased Tayena and mean marvellous. Both circumflexes remain, and l introduces an alternative.
Lhoſa completes marauilhoſa. This short row ends the marvellous-sense entry before the homograph for a cat.
This Meô is a cat, equated with Neco and Gato. It is a distinct sense despite identical visible accenting.
Meôcacu is the dignity or rank of a Buddha. Fotoque is a whole Japanese-derived term inside the Portuguese explanation; final Bup. is wholly upright.
Meôchi is excellent or marvellous wisdom, paraphrased Tayenaru chiye. The coordinated Portuguese description continues below.
Marauilhoſo ſaber completes the wisdom gloss. Final S. is the upright written-usage label, not italic explanation.

runs.text: Rol de varios nomes de homẽs.

lines.note: Meǒchǒ is a register of people’s names. The Portuguese has homẽs, not bomẽs, and both headword carons are retained.
Meǒchô means tomorrow morning. Both tildes belong over the second a in Amenhaã and manhaã. Final ô remains circumflexed, unlike the preceding entry’s ǒ.
Meôcu is an excellent phrase or saying, paraphrased Tayenaru cu. The Portuguese alternative follows below.
Ou dito completes the gloss as an excellent saying. This short row is not a new headword.

runs.text: Meôdo. Tayenaru tçuchi. i, Qidocuna to-

lines.note: Meôdo is a marvellous land or place, paraphrased Tayenaru tçuchi. The second paraphrase ends to-, not co-, forming Qidocuna tocoro below and matching Portuguese lugar.
Coro completes tocoro, “place,” not cocoro, “heart.” The Portuguese begins its comparison with the dwelling of Buddhas.

The comparison is with the place where the Buddhas are. Fotoques is a Japanese term within Portuguese explanatory prose and is marked for whole-word font review. Its small letterforms do not securely establish a contrast with the surrounding italics, so the input italic reading is retained as a nonblocking typeface uncertainty.
Meôfô is an excellent or marvellous law or teaching, paraphrased Tayenaru nori. Ma- begins marauilhoſa below.
Rauilhoſa completes marauilhoſa ley. This ends Meôfô before the longer title on the following row.
Meôfô rengueqiǒ is an invocation associated with the Lotus-school followers. Their name divides after Foc-; the ordinary headword itself is not a font-toggle term.

runs.text: quexùs, que he o titulo do liuro de Xaca chama

lines.note: Quexùs completes the followers’ name. The invocation is the title of a book of Xaca; chama continues below without a visible terminal hyphen. Xaca is embedded in the Portuguese explanation.
Do completes chamado, followed by Foquequiǒ. The book title’s final mark is a caron, not the OCR tilde; its printed spelling is not replaced with a normalized modern title.

runs.text: Olhos, ou ſaber claro com q̃

lines.note: Meǒgan is a Buddhist term for clear eyes or discerning knowledge. Q̃ is a Portuguese abbreviation introducing the explanation below.

runs.text: hũ penetra as couſas do Buppô, &c. ¶

lines.note: The discernment penetrates matters of the Buddhist teaching, Buppô. Its accent is circumflexed, not grave; Meǒ- begins the example and hũ remains unexpanded.
Ganno ſô completes Meǒganno ſô, a monk of clear understanding. Pe- continues as ra below, expressing the ability to penetrate the teaching.
Ra completes pera. Buppô again bears a circumflex rather than a grave and is a Japanese term within the Portuguese explanation.

runs.text: Couſa marauilhoſa q̃ não ſe pode facil-

lines.note: Meôjet is something marvellous that cannot readily be explained. Final t is retained; facil- begins the adverb below.
Mente completes facilmente explicar. Final S. is upright written-usage apparatus, separate from the italic translation.
Meôjut means marvellous or miraculous. It is distinct from Meôjet, and final S. is an upright usage label.
Meôni is a kitten, literally a cat’s offspring in the gloss. Its circumflex and upright S. label are retained.
Meôvon is an excellent voice, paraphrased Tayenaru coye. Excellente includes the vowel omitted in OCR Excllente.
Meqi supplies forms of a verb combining with nouns. The grammatical explanation runs across several rows rather than forming a simple noun definition.

runs.text: com algũs nomes, & ſignifica parecer, ou dar

lines.note: The combining verb means appearing or showing signs of something. ſignifica has f, not OCR j, and algũs retains its abbreviation.
Mostra completes dar mostra, “show signs.” Fitomequ exemplifies taking on a sensible person’s bearing; Mo- begins its translation below.
Strarſe completes Moſtrarſe: displaying a person’s sense and knowledge. Iro- starts the second compound example on this row.

runs.text: Aparecer muito, ou luzir algũa cor,

lines.note: Mequ completes Iromequ, here a colour’s conspicuous appearance or shining. The explanation continues with &c. before another compound.
Vaſamequ is glossed as conversing or talking. Praticar has its conversational sense here, with muito below qualifying the expression.
Muito completes the explanation as talking a great deal. This closes the compound examples, not the following sound-symbolic entry.

runs.text: Adu. Modo de ſoar algũa cou

lines.note: Meqi meqi is an adverb describing a cracking or creaking sound. The scan has Modo, not Medo; cou continues below without a secure terminal hyphen.

runs.text: ſa, como caſas, &c. com tremor da terra.

lines.note: Sa completes couſa. Houses making the sound during an earthquake give the example: structural noise, not fear of the structure.

runs.text: Peßoa que conhece muito polla viſta.

lines.note: Meqiqi is someone who recognizes or judges things well by sight. Its explanation continues at f317/c1-l001; isolated bottom i, que is the anticipatory catchword.
